name: Fabrinet
sector: Technology — precision optical / electronic contract manufacturing
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow. ROIC proxy (fundamentals.json) has held 14-20% for a decade — 17.5/18.3/19.2/19.8/18.1/18.7% across FY2021-26 — through the telecom downturn and COVID, which is real evidence of a process/qualification franchise: precision optical manufacturing is hard to replicate, OEM requalification is slow and risky, and Thailand scale gives a structural cost edge. But gross margin has been pinned at ~11-13% for ten years (12.0% in FY2026) — no pricing power against giant customers (top 4 = 57.4% of FY2026 revenue), and the high ROIC owes as much to a customer-funded, asset-turn model as to franchise. That combination is a 5, not a 7.
fragility_flags: OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share -0.84 vs 3-yr median 4.81 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 1.3% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.4x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: High-quality optical manufacturer (moat 5/10, ROIC ~19%) in an AI-datacenter supercycle, but at $372.48 the price capitalizes years of flawless growth: weighted IRR 5.7%, IV@15% $81 — it clears 15% only below ~$81; Tier D is a price verdict, not a business verdict.
moat_for: Precision optical process know-how + OEM qualification/switching costs — programs take years to qualify and are risky to move
ROIC proxy 14-20% every year for a decade (18.7% FY2026), held through the telecom downturn — returns above cost of capital through a cycle
Thailand scale/cost structure (Chonburi + Navanakorn campuses) that smaller rivals cannot match on complex optical builds
Deepening hyperscaler/OEM embed: four customers each >10% of revenue in FY2026 (Cisco 20%, NVIDIA 16%, Nokia 11%, Amazon 11%) and DCI run-rate above $1B
moat_against: No pricing power: gross margin ~12% and flat for a decade — the giant customers keep the economics
Customer concentration: top 4 = 57.4% of FY2026 revenue; losing or insourcing one program is a material hole
Single-geography manufacturing (Thailand) + China (Fuzhou): tariff, FX and tax exposure — Thailand Pillar Two top-up tax provision of $57.4M hit FY2026
Technology displacement risk: co-packaged optics / direct-drive architectures could bypass pluggable transceiver packaging
Contract manufacturing is ultimately replicable by scaled rivals (Jabil/Foxconn-class) if a customer funds the switch
